newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent, paper ease as four cargoes trade.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent, paper ease as four cargoes trade.

text.p: Dated Brent and intermonth paper spreads eased on Monday afternoon despite talk that a European major picked up four cargoes of the benchmark grade, traders said.
The cargoes were due to load between November 2 and 7 and were said to have fetched between Nov Brent plus 5 and 10 cents.
Details could not be confirmed immediately but traders said at least two of the cargoes were probably already committed.
The last reported wet Brent deal was on Friday at Nov Brent plus 11 cents for a Nov 4-6 loader.
Dec Brent paper lost five cents to $24.48 a barrel by 1533 GMT. The prompt Nov/Dec spread was pegged around +50 cents after trading at +53 cents.
The Dec/Jan spread was also softer, talking around +65/+70 cents after trading earlier at +73 cents.
Brent Contracts for Difference (CFDs) weakened, with next week's dates pegged at Dec Brent +50/+55 cents and Oct 28-Nov 01 at +25/+29 cents, dealers said.
"Next week's dates are being trashed," said a trader.
Both Monday's Brent cargoes, due to load Nov 5-7, were kept early by Total and Aron.
Other North Sea markets were quiet but some traders saw signs of a slight softening in premiums.
Forties was seen losing a couple of cents to Dated Brent +50/+55 cents and Norwegian Statfjord slipping to a similar degree to be valued around Dated Brent +60 cents.
"I don't see any real reason for the market to come off at the moment but it has gone a long way up so may be due a breather," said an equity producer.
Shell said its 80,000 barrels per day (bpd) Brent Charlie platform resumed production early on Monday after lengthy maintenance.
